title: BACE: Safety & Workplace Culture - Biotechnology - Waste Management
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: Where should a used glass slide containing a heat-fixed bacterial smear be disposed of?
questions.explain: Glass items contaminated with biological agents (like a bacterial smear) are considered biohazardous sharps. They must be disposed of in a rigid, puncture-resistant biohazard sharps container, not the clean broken glass box.
questions.subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: Biohazard bags are typically what color?
questions.explain: Red bags are the universal standard for biohazardous waste that requires decontamination (usually autoclaving) before disposal.
questions.subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: Ethidium Bromide (EtBr), a common DNA stain, is a known mutagen. How should agarose gels containing EtBr be disposed of?
options: Melted down and poured in the sink.
In a designated hazardous chemical solid waste container.
questions.explain: EtBr is a chemical hazard (mutagen), not a biohazard. It must go into a dedicated chemical waste container for incineration or hazardous disposal, not the regular trash or biohazard bags (unless the gel is also infectious, which is rare).
